answer: Coordination Velocity Pricing.** Each identity pays for the rate at which its actions align with others: when many fresh identities act in lockstep, a per-cluster fee rises sharply, like a trellis forcing separate vines apart. Honest agents acting independently stay cheap, while an attacker must either slow coordination (losing the sybil advantage) or pay escalating per-identity fees that grow with cluster size. Costs scale with synchronized breadth, not headcount, so a zephyr of scattered activity pays little, but a concentrated ocean of clones pays heavily.
